To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the response of wheat to inoculation with A. brasilense was variable and dependent on the interaction of the strain of bacterium and cultivar of wheat, growing season and N availability.

the response of wheat to inoculation with two A. brasilene strains was variable, and that nitrogen application increased the growth and grain yields of wheat, mainly in a site with low soil fertility.
wheat cultivar, growing environment, and inoculant strains are important factors that influence the response of wheat to A. brasilens e inoculation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a technology to increase grain production and quality, using biological nitrogen fixation by inoculating the seed with Azospirillium bacteria, in combination with the application of nitrogen fertilizers.

the evaluation of the response of wheat to the seed inoculation with strains of A. brasilense in environments that are representative of the Brazilian wheat production areas, with the aim to identify the best combination between wheat cultivar, A. brasiclense strains and nitrogen fertilization.
evaluating the response of wheat to inoculation with A. brasilense and N application in two environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
wheat inoculation with Azotobacter is a technology to be used with caution, as the responses to inoculation vary with the genotype, environment and management practices.

the response of wheat to inoculation with A.brasilense depends on several factors, and that the use of inoculation with A.brassilense is not recommended as a general practice for all cultivars, environments and nitrogen doses.
the use of inoculation with Azotobacter strains in the seeds of wheat is not yet an effective strategy to increase the productivity of this crop.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wheat cultivars showed different responses to seed inoculations with A. bralisense and nitrogen application, according to the environment and growing season.

the response of wheat to the seed inoculation with  A. brasilens e is variable, depending of the cultivar, environment and nitrogen availability, and the inoculation with A. brasilense can be a good alternative to reduce nitrogen application in wheat production.
the response of the wheat to inoculation with the strains Ab-V5 and Ab V6 of A. brascalense was variable according to the cultivars and environments evaluated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of wheat to inoculation with Azospirillum brasilense varies according to the genotype, growing season and environment.
the response of wheat to the inoculation with A.brassilense is cultivar-dependent.

the inoculation of wheat seeds with Azospirillium brasilense can be an alternative to increase the yield of this crop in low-fertility soils, but the results are dependent on the interaction with the cultivar, the environment and the nitrogen availability.
